rationale.conceptual: Standard but non-trivial method: DFT with PAW, symmetry-adapted strain states for elastic constants, DFPT phonon dispersion, QHA free energy integration from PHDOS and EDOS. Requires careful implementation and domain knowledge, but no novel algorithm; several interacting components.
rationale.execution: Multi-stage pipeline: geometry optimization, elastic constant calculations (multiple strain states), H2 reference, phonon DFPT, electronic DOS, and QHA post-processing across four phases. All steps are within Quantum ESPRESSO, but dependencies and orchestration of 6 stages make it a moderate engineering effort.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies standard DFT+QHA methods using Quantum ESPRESSO to compute elastic and thermodynamic properties of small unit cells. The conceptual difficulty is moderate: it requires understanding of solid-state physics, several interacting DFT components (strain-energy elastic constants, DFPT phonons, electronic DOS, QHA post-processing), but no novel algorithm. Execution involves a 6-step pipeline with dependencies, though mainly within one software suite. Resource needs are modest CPU-only calculations on tiny crystals.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small unit cells (max ~8 atoms) but many DFT calculations: geometry relaxations, elastic strain sets (~25 increments per strain), dense k‑grid SCF, DFPT with dense q‑grids, and DOS with tetrahedron method. Entirely CPU‑bound; a single multi‑core node with 64 GB RAM suffices.
